verification_report.summary:
The entire supplement was verified in textual order, including every proposition, source attribution, normalization, dimension endpoint and implication. It is correct under the expressly accepted manuscript inputs and the standing domain of smooth strictly positive probability measures. Ten statement records and five reference records contain the detailed checks.

The mass-invariance proof correctly uses small two-sided variations, polynomial coefficients, polarization and integration by parts. Complexifying real Hessian tests gives every complementary coordinate form, so the pointwise pairing detects every coefficient. The j=n-1 endpoint needs no remaining Hessian factors. The torsion identity has the stated plus sign and factors 2; in dimension two the degree-six torsion form vanishes automatically. Dimension one is separately covered by Stokes. Both cited statements and the polarization argument match [Chiose, Theorems 0.1–0.2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1609.05945v1).

Exact-background decreasing regularization and bounded Bedford–Taylor continuity correctly extend mass invariance and identify smooth and bounded extrema. For each fixed approximant, multiplication by 1-delta gives strict positivity and polynomial mass convergence; no uniform estimate in the approximant index is required. The accepted chapter26 proposition then gives density independence through normalized smooth Monge–Ampere measures.

The local gradient test is valid for every smooth real (n-1,n-1) form. Every complex covector alpha is the (1,0) part of the real covector alpha+bar(alpha), and df wedge dc f=(i/(2pi)) partial f wedge barpartial f. The cutoff error is O(k^(-1)); integration by parts makes the oscillatory integral vanish, leaving exactly one half of a strictly negative integral. This establishes precisely the stated positivity in that bidegree.

A local C2 extremum admits every individual smooth direction on an interval depending on that direction, including all oscillatory tests. First variation forces the Gauduchon condition. Second variation is exactly -n(n-1) integral df wedge dc f wedge ddc(Omega^(n-2)); the sign follows from Stokes and closedness of ddc(Omega^(n-2)). The gradient test therefore proves the necessary nonpositive sign at minima and nonnegative sign at maxima.

In dimension three the exact quadratic mass identity has coefficient -3. Its sign proves both local/global/geometric equivalences. Approximation gives the asserted attained bounded-potential values v_- and v_+, with a finite v_+ in the maximum case. In the minimum case gamma=Omega attains the Gauduchon infimum: its quotient equals (integral Omega^3)^(1/3). The Hopf minimum is 6 under the accepted normalization, compatibly with infinite upper mass. On surfaces the affine mass has a local extremum exactly when omega is Gauduchon.

The required theorem search found Chiose directly; AGL was confirmed by subsequent web search and the supplied published text. Definition 3.1 specializes in dimension three to exactly the Gauduchon and plurinegative hypotheses, and the proof gives the cited sufficient lower-bound identity. The terminology and attribution match [Angella–Guedj–Lu, Theorem 3.2, pp. 4641–4642](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~guedj/fichierspdf/TAMS22.pdf). Rescaling the reference potential by 1/(2pi) reconciles operators and preserves the coefficient -3, all zero conditions and all signs. No all-dimensional sufficiency, BMP assumption, general existence of an extremizer or unsupported novelty claim is used.
